subject: Staging readiness signal request + temporary pin exception for Polaris-7b-compact
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com; BrightPath Integrations <integrations@brightpath.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Staging readiness signal request + temporary pin exception for Polaris-7b-compact

Team —

Quick ask to align today on the staging signal and a short-lived pin exception for the Polaris-7b-compact variant BrightPath will promote to production next week. Summary: BrightPath ran a full pass in their sandbox yesterday; they hit a couple of prompt regressions that engineering fixed overnight. They want a conservative rollout, and they have requested we hold production on the current variant until we complete one final canary.

What I need from us:
- Product: confirmation of the readiness signal criteria (latency, top-1 safety heuristics, hallucination rate delta).
- Eng (runtime): a recommended temporary pin window (how long we can pin without blocking other rollouts) and the rollback criteria we will use if telemetry worsens.
- CS/partner-facing: a short message we can send BrightPath that sets expectations and their responsibilities for canary monitoring.

Why this is unusual: Polaris-7b-compact is smaller but uses a new compilation path in the runtime. The staging smoke report (attached) shows a ~5% token-cost improvement but a 0.8% increase in rare hallucination signals on long-form prompts. We need a clear, cross-functional decision so we don't ship silently.

Proposed near-term plan (my thinking):
1) Approve a 72-hour temporary pin to the existing polaris-7b-compact-v1 for BrightPath production traffic.
2) During those 72 hours we run a canary at 5% traffic with the new variant; if specific telemetry triggers fire (see rollback draft), we immediately fail the canary and keep v1 pinned.
3) Post-72 hours: either roll forward or remove the pin based on the canary outcome.

Attachments: polaris-staging-smoke-20260821.pdf (smoke run), rollback-criteria-draft-20260822.md (draft runbook).

Can you reply with 1) a yes/no on the 72-hour pin, 2) any changes to the rollback triggers, and 3) the short customer note you want me to send?

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: BrightPath Integrations <integrations@brightpath.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staging readiness signal request + temporary pin exception for Polaris-7b-compact

Jordan —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifying questions before I sign off on the 72-hour pin:

1) Which exact telemetry do we treat as "hallucination signals"? The attachment calls out two detectors (context-contradiction and entity-invented) — do both have to trip, or is either sufficient?
2) Latency SLO: what's the 95th percentile delta we're willing to accept for the canary vs. baseline?
3) Does the proposed pin block other scheduled rollouts that week if an urgent fix comes in? We need to ensure marketplace fairness across customers.

Also: I want the customer-facing note to explicitly state that this is a precautionary pin and that we will provide hourly canary updates for the first 12 hours, with a summary at 72 hours. Tone: concise, accountable.

If engineering can answer the telemetry thresholds and confirm the isolation policy, I'm fine approving the temporary pin window.

-Laura
Sr Product Manager, Model Governance
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: BrightPath Integrations <integrations@brightpath.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staging readiness signal request + temporary pin exception for Polaris-7b-compact

Laura / Jordan —

Short answers and proposed technical runbook:

1) Hallucination signals: we should treat either detector tripping above threshold as actionable. Concretely: context-contradiction rate > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline OR entity-invented > 0.3% absolute increase triggers an immediate fail (stop canary). Both are listed in the attached rollback-criteria-draft-20260822.md.

2) Latency SLOs: Acceptable delta is +15ms p95 compared to baseline variant. The smoke run shows p95 delta of +9ms for the new compilation path — within tolerance.

3) Pin isolation: engineering can isolate the pin to BrightPath's tenant routing only. This pin will not block other customers or scheduled rollouts unless we explicitly broaden it.

Recommended operational plan (what we'll run):
- Approve 72-hour tenant-scoped pin for polaris-7b-compact-v1.
- Immediately start a 5% canary (new variant) for BrightPath traffic with 1-min aggregation windows into our telemetry engine.
- Monitoring: hourly alerts for the first 12 hours (auto-summary), then 4-hour cadence thereafter. Critical trigger = either hallucination detector threshold OR latency > +30ms sustained for 10 minutes.
- Rollback: automatic traffic cut to v1 + incident page opened; eng on-call paged; notify CS and product.

Attachment: polaris-staging-smoke-20260821.pdf (results) — key note: cost gains are visible on medium-length prompts, but the rare hallucination delta is concentrated in >1024-token sessions.

I'm comfortable with the 72-hour pinned window given tenant-scoping and the auto-rollback triggers above.

-Dev
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lin <sara@brightpath.ai>

Cc: integrations@brightpath.ai

Subject: Re: Staging readiness signal request + temporary pin exception for Polaris-7b-compact

Jordan / Laura / Dev —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear plan. BrightPath accepts the tenant-scoped 72-hour pin and the proposed canary/runbook. We'll:
- Kick off canary at 10:00 PT tomorrow (we'll send the first hour report).
- Share any customer-reported anomalies to the integration address immediately.
- Expect hourly updates for the first 12 hours, then summaries as you outlined.

Please send the customer-facing note and the pinned-variant confirmation so our ops team can finalize the cutover checklist.

Best,
Sara Lin
Head of AI Integration
BrightPath AI
